result.rule: Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.

result.rule: When the description states that an action performed by one participant sends a message to another participant, or that another participant's start or wait point depends on that action, whether the other participant is a peer in the process or an external party acting on its own: Model each participant as its own pool in one collaboration. Draw every cross-participant dependency as a message flow from the sending participant's task (or throw event) to a message start event or intermediate message catch event in the receiving participant's pool. Do not connect elements of different pools with sequence flows. Do not connect a sending task to a catch event inside the same pool with a message flow. Do not reverse the flow so that the receiving start or catch event is the source.

When the description states that one participant sends a document or decision to another participant as a plain step that the receiver then acts on, and it gives no message content, no response to wait for, and no pool-to-pool exchange: Model the sending step as a plain task in the sender's lane, not as a send task. Use a send task only when the description makes the message emission itself the unit of work, for example by giving its content or requiring a message flow to a receiver in another pool.

When the description states that one participant sends requests for proposals to several outside parties and then chooses one of them, and does not state that those parties run their own processes or act as independent participants in the interaction: Model the outreach to the outside parties and the later choice of one of them as tasks and a decision inside the lane of the participant who performs them. Do not create a pool for those outside parties, and do not add message flows to or from them, unless the description states that they act as independent participants with their own behaviour.

When the description says that while an ongoing processing activity is under way, a party is repeatedly given intermediate updates and the flow then continues with further steps: Model each such intermediate update as a task (a send task if the update is a message being sent) placed inside the sequence flow of the ongoing activity, with the flow continuing afterwards. Do not model an update as an end event, because an end event marks only a terminal outcome of the process.

Do not model the idle period as a task, because a task represents work the participant performs, and an idle period contains no work.
